title: Multi-Task Learning in Natural Language Processing: An Overview
problem_statement: Deep neural models and pre-trained language models in natural language processing frequently encounter overfitting, data scarcity, and excessive computational adaptation costs when researchers train the models on isolated downstream tasks.
domain: Natural Language Processing, Multi-Task Learning, Deep Learning, Pre-trained Language Models
theoretical_framework: Multi-Task Learning (MTL) principles wherein sharing inductive bias and complementary representations across related tasks improves model generalization and reduces sample complexity compared to isolated single-task learning.
methodology: A comprehensive literature review and taxonomic categorization analyzing multi-task learning across four primary architectural paradigms (parallel, hierarchical, modular, and generative adversarial), multi-task optimization strategies (loss construction, gradient regularization, data sampling, and task scheduling), downstream application areas (auxiliary MTL and joint MTL), and benchmark datasets.
key_findings: Multi-task learning architectures in natural language processing divide systematically into parallel architectures, hierarchical architectures, modular architectures, and generative adversarial architectures.

Modular multi-task learning mechanisms, including parameter-efficient adapters, prefix tuning, and hypernetworks, attain performance comparable to full model fine-tuning while reducing trainable parameter counts and storage requirements.

Optimization techniques such as uncertainty-based sampling, dynamic task scheduling, and gradient regularization prevent catastrophic forgetting and mitigate negative transfer across heterogeneous tasks.

Task relatedness substantially influences multi-task learning outcomes, where auxiliary tasks with high label entropy and balanced distributions provide greater performance gains than unrelated tasks.
Multi-task learning effectively alleviates data scarcity in low-resource languages and specialized domains by transferring shared representations from data-rich auxiliary tasks.
scope_and_delimitations: The authors focus specifically on the application of multi-task learning to downstream natural language processing tasks rather than general pre-training objectives.
The authors restrict the architectural taxonomy primarily to multi-task models containing task-specific trainable parameters, excluding general instruction tuning without task-specific parameters.
The authors examine deep learning approaches and exclude non-neural multi-task learning methods.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: Firstly, given multiple NLP tasks, how to find a set of tasks that could take advantage of MTL remains a challenge. Besides improving performance of MTL models, a deeper understanding of task relatedness could also help expanding the application of MTL to more tasks. Though there are some works studying this issue, as discussed in Section 4.4, they are far from mature.
limitations.summary: The authors identify that determining optimal task combinations and establishing a formal understanding of task relatedness remain immature and unresolved challenges in multi-task learning.

generalizability_gap: Existing research evaluates multi-task learning primarily on high-resource languages and standard benchmark tasks, leaving multi-task transfer in low-resource languages, multimodal environments, and interactive dialogue systems under-explored.
methodological_gap: Current large pre-trained language models predominantly employ basic feature-sharing architectures during training, and existing task selection heuristics lack standardized quantitative metrics and theoretical guarantees across diverse task spaces.
future_work: Developing theoretical and empirical frameworks to quantify task relatedness and systematically select beneficial task combinations.
Incorporating self-supervised and unsupervised learning techniques into multi-task learning to exploit unlabeled data and reduce dependence on human annotations.
Designing advanced multi-task architectures beyond simple feature sharing to improve pre-trained language models.
Extending multi-task learning to complex downstream applications, including dialogue systems and multimodal vision-language tasks.
